title: Santo in Chicago and the theater agent's office
summary: Lala tells how a trombonist from New Orleans looked him up in Chicago, got work, and embarrassed Lala by asking a theater agent about putting a band on stage.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: You mean the man, somebody knocked on his door? Santo Piccolo? Somebody knocked on his head or something. I had something with me. Mr. Tailgate you mean? Yeah. I don't know what the other call is that. I had something with me. The price of fame, huh? I was in Chicago.
I'm sleeping one morning, who comes in there knocking on the door with Santa? Come on.
Santo Snark and all Johnny's. Yeah.

Yeah, he comes to look me up in Chicago. You know, he was in Beloxi with Joe Pooker. He had a big humbug with his wife and everything. He's like. He's like. So I was working in the town. So I went to work that night. He came with me and everything. You know, I introduced him around. So he had a good trombone player with me and everything. So finally, the leader called me inside and said, would you like something? Work with you. I said, I like it. I worked $15 a week cheaper. No, no, not then. No, that time you're old. But we're getting $20 a week. No, no, no, no. We're getting $125, bud. Oh, no. I'm just kidding, John. I'm not kidding. I'm kidding. I'm kidding. Down here. Oh, I was working down here for $12 a week. Wasn't making $15, $18, $20 a night dips though. We was getting down every night down here. And making $15, $20 a night dips. Yeah, down here. I'm still kidding about Santa. I bet you Santa went in there and tried to own a little bit of money.
No, no, no, no, no, no.

That was all by booking agent by, you know? That goes by my ugly, suspicious mindless dear. So finally what happened, I said to him, he said, well, I can play so-and-so some ways. He won't be out of a job. He leaves tonight, he goes and we'll wait tomorrow night. So they asked him and so they said, you know, them boys work together. The only thing I worked with him, I had him bone for me when he was running, but I thought he had to work. First he comes to work and we're getting $125 a piece, $250 of brass to him, him and I. I said, Sons, one thing you got to do is keep your mantra. Don't talk. If you got anything to say, let me know what you're going to say before you say that. One day, I'll never forget this one was out there, we went to the show and we worked and got a good job. He said, well, I want to go see somebody. I said, where you want to go see? Come on. So he brought me up from Chicago. He said, Chicago, McGarry Theater building. Man, way up on the top floor. But if I knew he was going up there, I would never went for him. He goes, he sees the sign and then I forget this name as long as I lived because I felt so embarrassed. Mr. Ford, who can entertain him and the musician. The doctor goes to the office and says, Mr. Ford? I'm behind him, you know. He says, well, I want to come see about putting the band on the stage. I looked at him, you know. I said, Jesus Christ. I was going up there. The man said, well, what's the name of your band? He said, well, I ain't got no band yet. He says, I'm from New Orleans. I used to work in the Palace Theater and he used to throw the spotlight on me. So the man he looked at me and I looked at the man, I told the man, I was walking. He walked out. So the man said, well, when you get your band on me here, I'm going to get a band up. But when we got down, outside I was way down to the Hall of Plum. I'd give him more devil. I raised all the time he came up. I said, well, if I knew you was going up there to make a fool out yourself, I wasn't mad. He'd take you crazy. He knows you crazy. He'd take I crazy. He'd take you for good with you. But I wasn't mad. I wouldn't go down the elevator. I took a walk down and five steps. And that night I was so angry that I wanted to go. I went to the office and said, John, you make a fool out yourself. Keep your mind shut. You wouldn't keep your mind shut. That's not the same way now, but I bet it's the same way now. I bet it's the same way now.
